data.narrative:
Ursa Major Technologies is a Series E-stage space and aerospace company that has raised $85M to date. The valuation landscape includes 5 public peers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private comparables including SpaceX and Sierra Space, though a sufficiently dense same-stage private peer set does not exist within the narrow filters applied.

Given data limitations, only the stage-progression method is applicable. Using total capital raised as a proxy base of $85M and applying a typical 1.4x step-up multiplier from Series E to subsequent funding stages yields an implied valuation of $119M. The public-comp anchoring approach cannot be deployed without disclosed revenue figures, which private companies typically do not provide. The peer-median approach lacks the minimum three datapoints required in the same-stage cohort (only one adjacent-stage comparable identified among 11 same-sector peers).

The analysis supports a valuation range of $101M to $137M, centered on $119M. This range reflects methodological constraints rather than precision: with only one applicable triangulation method, the low and high bounds represent ±15% sensitivity adjustments around the median rather than independent corroboration. Material uncertainties include the absence of revenue-based anchoring and a thin comparable set at this stage in the space sector. Revenue disclosure and closer Stage E peer data would materially improve conviction in any final valuation.
